method_finding.headline: VALIDATED_IVP_INTEGRATION_IS_NOT_REQUIRED
method_finding.derivation: AS_EXACT performs a fixed ten-step recursion with no adaptivity, no step control and no error estimate. Given an enclosure of DLR the whole computation is a finite composition of additions, subtractions and multiplications, so ordinary interval evaluation already encloses every value the recursion can produce.
method_finding.what_it_does_not_claim: The enclosure bounds the recursion's own output. It says nothing about the exact solution of the beta-function differential equation, and the two are not the same object.
method_finding.consequence_for_v3: The provisional V3 design and this task's brief both anticipated interval Runge-Kutta with a local truncation bound or Taylor-model integration. Neither is needed, because the frozen target is the algorithm rather than the differential equation.

evidence.toy_demonstration: fixed_step_rk4_enclosure over a toy cubic right-hand side contained all 401 binary64 replay points at every subdivision level, and the enclosure overshoot fell from 1.0749 to 1.0003 as the partition went from 1 to 256 cells.

a5_apfel_continuous_enclosure.remaining_gap: DLR is DLOG(MU2/MU20) from the platform libm, so the same logarithm gap applies.

a6_consistency_claim.why_not_exact_identity: CT18 exposes a cubic Hermite interpolation of serialized values with a magnitude clamp; APFEL exposes a ten-step fixed RK4 recursion with a truncated one-sixth literal. These are different finite algorithms and are not the same mathematical function, so exact identity is not the right claim and could never pass.
a6_consistency_claim.why_unresolved: A bounded-consistency claim needs a level. The accepted records supply none: the massless 1e-5 and MassiveDIS 0.001 figures are comparator-local and explicitly non-transferable, machine epsilon is not a physics requirement, and the research-question record selects no metric and declares no event-set size or calibration tolerance.

libm_finding.why_it_matters: Both providers evaluate a natural logarithm, and the accepted sign contract makes the actual implemented finite-precision object the load-bearing one. Enclosing an idealised real-arithmetic function is therefore not sufficient.

evidence.retrieval_qualification: Retrieved from the bminor/glibc GitHub mirror at tag glibc-2.39, not from sourceware directly; the hash identifies the retrieved bytes, and a successor that relies on this bound should re-retrieve from the upstream repository.
evidence.finding: The source states a worst-case error around 0.507 ULP on the near-one path and 0.519 ULP with fma or 0.520 ULP without fma otherwise. These are the implementers' own error analysis, not a machine-checked proof.

The x86_64 symbol is an ifunc selected at load time among sse2, avx, fma4 and fma variants, and the source itself documents different rounding for the fma and non-fma paths. The mathematical function realised by log therefore depends on the CPU.
The inspection host advertises fma and avx2, so it would select an fma variant. A host without fma would select a different one and could return different bits.

libm_finding.consequence: A rigorous enclosure of either implemented provider requires either an interval re-implementation of the selected libm routine including its lookup tables, or acceptance of a declared and clearly qualified ULP bound together with a frozen CPU feature set. Neither is established by the accepted records.
libm_finding.guard_implemented: declared_ulp_log_enclosure refuses to widen an enclosure unless both a numeric bound and a stated authority are supplied.

c1_requirement_decision.question: does authorization require a rigorous quadrature remainder certificate, or a predeclared empirical convergence rule with an independent cross-check

c1a_assessment.derivation: A rigorous remainder needs an integrand that can be evaluated in interval arithmetic, or at least a certified bound on a derivative of known order. The accepted integrand is the frozen APFEL FONLL-A binary64 rate wrapper. It exposes one binary64 number per point and no interval extension, no derivative enclosure and no modulus of continuity. No verified quadrature method, including interval Gauss rules, validated adaptive quadrature and Arb ball integration, can be applied to such a black box.
c1a_assessment.consequence: Requiring C1A would require replacing the accepted implementation, which the accepted records forbid for the same reason AS1 was rejected.

c1b_assessment.reason: An empirical rule is implementable, but it needs a declared precision target, and no accepted record supplies one.

c2_rigorous_route.common_precondition: an interval-extensible integrand or a certified derivative bound
c2_rigorous_route.conclusion: No rigorous integration method can be predeclared for the future DIS integrand while the integrand remains a binary64 black box.

c3_empirical_route.attempted_derivation: The load-bearing object is the normalized selected-event law q = r / Z. A relative error in Z biases the per-event log density, and over an event set of size N the bias on the log posterior scales like N times that relative error. A sufficient accuracy for Z therefore follows from a declared event-set size and a declared acceptable posterior or coverage distortion.
why_it_fails: The accepted research-question record fixes no event-set size N for the planned study.
It explicitly states that no information-content or calibration metric is selected.
It declares no acceptable coverage or calibration distortion.
The MassiveDIS 0.001 and massless 1e-5 levels are comparator-local and may not be reused as a project target.

counterexample.purpose: test whether successive-difference agreement, or independent cross-rule agreement, bounds the remainder
counterexample.function: exp(-((x-c)/w)^2) on [-1,1], an entire function, with c = 0.1824 and w = 1e-4
counterexample.node_separation: c is at least 0.01269 away from every node of Gauss-Legendre 16, 32 and 64 and Clenshaw-Curtis 17, 33 and 65

mpmath.role: pinned diagnostic only, never a rigorous backend

native_code_identity.reason: The x86_64 log symbol is resolved by an ifunc at load time from the CPU feature set, so the numerical function realised depends on the host CPU and not only on the pinned software versions.

workstream_d_environment.bitwise_claim_reason: Bitwise reproducibility would require a frozen CPU feature set in addition to frozen software, because the selected libm variant and its documented rounding differ between fma and non-fma hosts.
workstream_d_environment.why_not_numerically_reproducible_with_fr: That weaker classification asserts that freezing the software identity determines the numbers. The ifunc finding shows it does not: the same frozen LHAPDF, APFEL and glibc versions realise different logarithms on hosts with and without fma. The claim would also need a declared agreement tolerance, and no accepted record supplies one, so it is not a checkable statement. The honest classification is therefore unresolved rather than the weaker positive one.

non_dis_validation_evidence.authorized_scope: interval backend toy containment, validated arithmetic on toy recursions, quadrature exact-integral tests, grid nesting tests, rigor guards
results: A toy fixed-step RK4 recursion enclosure contained all 401 binary64 replay points at 1, 4, 16, 64 and 256 cells, with the overshoot falling from 1.0749 to 1.0003.
A Hermite cubic enclosure over 32 cells contained all 2001 binary64 replay points.
The magnitude clamp classifier returned BELOW, AT_OR_ABOVE and UNDECIDED on the three intended cases.
The rigor guard accepted python-flint.arb and mpfi and rejected mpmath, mpmath.iv, math, numpy, decimal and an unknown name.
The declared-ulp logarithm helper refused a missing bound, an empty justification and a negative bound.
The 17/33/65 geometric grids are bitwise nested on both axes; 16/32/64 is not.
The convergence verdict helper refused a missing target, an empty justification, a zero target and an infinite target.
Gauss-Legendre and Clenshaw-Curtis reproduced exact polynomial and exponential integrals and converged on a smooth rational; both stalled badly on a near-endpoint pole.
On an entire narrow-bump integrand both rules returned exactly zero at all three levels while the exact integral is 1.7725e-4.
non_dis_validation_evidence.toy_literal_note: The truncated one-sixth literal shifted the toy recursion midpoint by 1.31e-17, which is inside that configuration's 2.33e-16 accumulated rounding envelope. The literal is a real deviation from one sixth and matters for any bitwise-replay claim, but this toy configuration does not by itself demonstrate a numerically significant effect.

outcome.derivation: Workstream A resolved the exact provider mathematics, the 4*pi convention and the interval backend, and eliminated the validated-IVP requirement, but the implemented-function enclosure and the consistency criterion remain unresolved. Workstream B bound the MassiveDIS executable identity and recovered the massless reference configuration, yet no independent FONLL-A comparator is bound and the massless candidate side is unbound. Workstream C established that a rigorous remainder is not implementable against the accepted black-box integrand and that no project precision target exists to anchor the empirical alternative. Workstream D could not bind the libm identity. Three blocker families therefore remain.

blockers_remaining.missing: a rigorous enclosure of the platform natural logarithm invoked by both providers, together with a frozen CPU feature set
blockers_remaining.would_be_resolved_by: either an interval re-implementation of the selected glibc log routine including its tables, or an accepted decision to certify against a declared and qualified ULP bound on a frozen CPU

blockers_remaining.missing: a defensible nonzero consistency level, or an accepted decision to replace the threshold with propagation plus reference-closure gates
blockers_remaining.would_be_resolved_by: a declared project precision target, or reference-closure gates that can actually pass

blockers_remaining.missing: an executable independent FONLL-A comparator with a matched configuration and an acceptance rule
blockers_remaining.would_be_resolved_by: an authoritative APFEL-to-MassiveDIS scheme correspondence plus a declared precision target, or a published table with exact coordinates for a reproducible configuration

blockers_remaining.missing: frozen APFEL 3.1.1 grid and interpolation settings, a bridge contract covering a sqrt(2) GeV boundary, and a finite work cap
blockers_remaining.would_be_resolved_by: serializing those settings and extending the bridge contract to a second boundary configuration

blockers_remaining.missing: a declared accuracy requirement for the normalized simulator law
blockers_remaining.would_be_resolved_by: declaring the event-set size and an acceptable posterior or coverage distortion, from which an accuracy for Z follows, or removing the normalization-accuracy claim from the paper boundary

blockers_remaining.missing: a gate whose quantity is scientifically meaningful
blockers_remaining.would_be_resolved_by: replacing the refinement gate with the exact coverage and nesting audit in a successor plan

blockers_remaining.missing: an executable interpreter, libm and CPU feature identity
blockers_remaining.would_be_resolved_by: freezing a container image with a pinned CPU feature baseline and recording the resolved ifunc selection

outcome.why_no_authorization_review: Three load-bearing blocker families remain and every reference-closure gate is still unable to pass. An authorization review conducted now could only restate the same blockers.
outcome.why_no_v4: V4 may exist only if BR1 is independently and positively established. It was not. Creating a successor plan now would present unresolved specifications as complete.

remaining_scientific_limitations: No end-to-end independent implementation of the complete NC rate exists.
No independent executable FONLL-A comparator is bound.
The massless candidate-side execution specification is incomplete.
The alpha certification cannot enclose the implemented providers because the platform logarithm is unbound.
No rigorous quadrature remainder is obtainable against the accepted black-box integrand.
No accepted project precision target exists, so no empirical convergence rule can be anchored.
Successive-difference and cross-rule agreement are demonstrated not to bound a remainder.
Finite point grids do not prove continuum positivity.
Nine theta anchors do not establish every interior theta.
Inclusive NC electron-proton data do not provide unrestricted flavour separation.
No alpha, bridge, DIS, sign, convergence, normalization or closure result was executed.
next_step: Decide the two questions that gate everything else: whether the project will certify against a declared and qualified platform-logarithm bound on a frozen CPU, and what accuracy the normalized simulator law actually requires. Both are scientific decisions about the claim, not further source review. Until they are recorded, a successor preauthorization plan cannot be complete and no authorization review is warranted.
